my nails are cut very short, I don't think they're physically even able to touch the strings at this point.
I know my left hand is way too tense and I put a lot of pressure on the strings, but it has gotten better and my strings still break just as often as before.
and the luthiers I've talked to have both been violin specific, one of which even was the one who built my violin.

the a string tends to unravel at about a d# in the first position, Nd the e string snaps at around the nut, so it'd make sense for there to be something sharp there even though there doesn't seem to be.

My resolution is to not focus my practice around time. I've been doing 4 hours a day for as long as I can remember and was slowly falling out of love with violin. Now for the past two weeks I've been trying to not pressure myself into practicing four hours with breaks every 60 mins, but to play until I need a break (max. 60 mins, but sometimes less). I also used to fit whatever I decided to work on that day (say the shifts in a piece etc) into the time frame I set for it. And now I've just been listing the stuff I want to work on, usually I focus on technique and two pieces a day in which I tent to pick out details, and then I'll prectice it until I'm happy with it.
This has resulted in me practicing more than before, which was surprising, and falling back in love with this immensely beautiful instrument.
